name: Polenta e Funghi

ingredients.name: vegetarian hard grating cheese made with vegetarian coagulants

steps: Check that the grated hard cheese is made with vegetarian coagulants. Bring 1250 ml water and 7 g salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan. Whisk in the coarse polenta in a slow stream to avoid lumps. Reduce to a very gentle simmer and cook for 35–40 minutes, stirring frequently and scraping the bottom, until the grains are tender and the mixture is thick but spoonable. Add a little hot water if it stiffens too soon.
While the polenta cooks, brush the mushrooms clean and slice thickly. Mince garlic, strip the thyme leaves and chop parsley. Heat 25 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat.

Brown mushrooms in two batches so they do not steam, leaving each batch undisturbed for 2 minutes before turning. Cook another 4–5 minutes until their released liquid has evaporated and the edges are deeply golden. Return all mushrooms to the pan, add garlic and thyme and cook 45 seconds. Add 4 g salt and black pepper, stir for 1 minute, then take off the heat; a little natural mushroom pan juice is welcome.

When the polenta grains are fully tender, turn off the heat and stir in the remaining 20 g butter and 30 g finely grated vegetarian cheese. Beat for 1 minute until glossy and creamy. The polenta should slowly spread when spooned into a bowl; loosen with a splash of hot water if needed.

Spoon the hot golden polenta into four shallow bowls. Pile the browned mushrooms and any pan juices over each portion. Sprinkle with chopped parsley, the remaining 15 g cheese and a little thyme. Serve immediately before the polenta sets.
tips: The reviewed image shows a clearly visible bed of soft yellow polenta topped with richly browned mushrooms, herbs and a small cheese garnish. Use coarse polenta for the stated simmer time; instant polenta needs its packet timing instead. Mushroom browning and loose spoonable polenta are the key textures.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
